card.architecture: Anima finetune (Cosmos-Predict2-derived 2B, Qwen3-0.6B encoder, Qwen-Image VAE)
card.summary: Photographic finetune of Anima Base v1.0 (same 2B architecture), trained ~45k steps on ~2000 highly-aesthetic photos. THIS entry is the de-turbo'd build: the baked-in Anima Turbo LoRA was subtracted back out, so it runs at full quality (~40 steps, CFG ~4) instead of Turbo's few-step / CFG-1 path. Strong prompt adherence, stable anatomy, up to ~2MP; amateur/candid realism. Non-commercial.
card.pick_when: Fast, realistic, candid-style photos from a lightweight 2B model; non-commercial OK. De-turbo'd -- uses normal CFG/steps, not the Turbo few-step path.

prompt.overview: De-turbo'd photographic finetune of Anima (2B): plain natural-language photo prompts with a quality/realism prefix auto-prepended. Run at ~40 steps, er_sde sampler, simple scheduler, CFG ~4.
prompt.instructions:
This is the DE-TURBO'D Photanima (the baked-in Anima Turbo LoRA was removed), so use the base-model recipe: ~40 steps, er_sde sampler, 'simple' scheduler, CFG ~4 -- NOT the Turbo 6-8 step / CFG 1 / custom-sigma path.
Write plain, specific photographic descriptions (subject, setting, lighting, lens, mood). Amateur/candid language helps realism (e.g. 'amateur smartphone photo', 'visible grain', 'natural skin texture').
The quality/realism fluff prefix ('masterpiece, score_9, absurdres, best quality, highres, photo \(medium\), real life,') is prepended AUTOMATICALLY for this base/non-turbo build -- do NOT type it. For extra realism you can prepend a stronger weighted '(photo \(medium\):3)' (the model tolerates strengths up to ~5-6 before breaking).
Do NOT add further hype tags (hyperreal, etc.) beyond the auto prefix -- the model is photographic and aesthetic by default and over-driving fries the image.
Anatomy is stable; if something glitches, nudge steps +/-1. Supports up to ~2MP (preferred 832x1216 or 1040x1520) with little distortion. In-image text is weak beyond 3-4 words. Micro-detail is between SDXL and Z-Image -- a touch of film grain, or refining the output in another model, helps.
do: Write a plain, specific photographic description (subject, setting, lighting, lens, mood)
Use amateur/candid photo language for realism (grain, natural skin, smartphone photo)
Let the app add the quality/realism prefix -- don't type it
For more realism, prepend a stronger '(photo \(medium\):3)', or just add a little film grain
Keep any in-image text to 3-4 words
dont: Pile on hype/quality tags beyond the auto prefix (it fries the image)
Use the Turbo settings (6-8 steps / CFG 1 / custom sigma) -- this build is de-turbo'd
Rely on niche art terms like 'silhouette'
examples: amateur smartphone photo of a young woman by a white van in a sunlit pine forest, dappled light, natural skin texture, visible grain, candid, medium shot
candid 35mm photo of an elderly fisherman mending a net on a weathered dock at golden hour, soft side light, shallow depth of field
prompt.negative_guidance: CFG ~4, so negatives work but keep them light (the model is aesthetic by default). e.g. 'worst quality, low quality, jpeg artifacts'.

negative.note: Works at CFG ~4; keep it light -- aesthetic by default.
